name: Mangalia
title: Ship Thickness Measurement in Mangalia | UTM & Hull Gauging
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Mangalia for ships at the shipyard or alongside: hull, tank and deck gauging, pre-docking UTM and survey support.
h1: Hull Gauging and UTM for Ships Calling at Mangalia, Romania
intro: Mangalia is the southernmost Romanian port, a short run from the Bulgarian border and built around a large shipyard rather than a cargo terminal. Ships that come here are mostly there for repair, conversion, lay-up or a sale inspection. A gauging team travels from India to join the ship at the yard or alongside, measures the structure against the survey scope and leaves the superintendent with figures that can be put into a repair specification.

highlights.p: Most ships reach Mangalia because of the shipyard, so gauging usually sits inside a repair or conversion programme. Measuring on arrival gives the yard, the owner and the class surveyor one measured set of figures when the steel scope is agreed.

With little commercial cargo work, ships at Mangalia often lie for days with tanks empty and ventilated. That leaves room for a methodical measurement grid on deck, shell and tank boundaries without cargo gear or stevedores in the way.

Constanța lies to the north and Varna to the south, both within reach by road. A fleet with ships in the area can group calls on a single mobilisation from India instead of travelling for each ship separately.

port.h: Mangalia: a shipyard port on the southern Romanian coast
p: Mangalia sits on the open Black Sea coast in the far south of Romania, a resort town as well as a port. Its harbour is protected by breakwaters, and the approach is straightforward compared with the Danube ports, with no river bar to cross and no canal to transit. The commercial role of the port is small beside Constanța. What defines Mangalia is the shipyard on the harbour front, with its long quays and heavy-lift capacity, which has historically built offshore units and large hulls as well as repairing ships.

Traffic is therefore irregular rather than steady. A ship may arrive for a conversion, a major repair, a long period alongside while its future is decided, or simply to wait for a yard slot. Offshore support vessels, dredgers and naval auxiliaries appear from time to time, and so do larger merchant ships that need a quay and cranes more than they need a cargo berth. The Romanian Navy also keeps a base in the town, which means some parts of the waterfront are not available for commercial work.

Weather matters on this coast more than tides do. The Black Sea has a negligible tidal range, so waterline and freeboard readings stay stable, but winter gales from the north and east can stop launch boardings at an anchorage and make work on exposed decks unpleasant. Spring and summer are the easy months for outdoor gauging of decks and hatch covers, while autumn and winter jobs are best planned for the sheltered inside berths and for tank and hold work, which does not depend on the weather.

facilities.h: Where gauging can happen at Mangalia
p: The shipyard is the place to measure a ship properly. Ownership and operating arrangements at the yard have changed in recent years, so before planning a docking the superintendent should confirm with the ship's agent which company is running the facility, what dock and quay capacity is actually available and what access rules apply to outside contractors. If a docking is booked, gauging in the first days gives the steel list a measured basis, with bottom shell, bilge, sea chests and the lower side shell open to the gauge.

A ship that is not in dock can still be gauged alongside. At a quiet berth the deck, hatch coamings, air pipes, ballast tank boundaries and cargo spaces that are empty can be measured without interrupting anything. Where an owner wants bottom plating measured and no dry dock is free at Mangalia, the realistic plan is to gauge what is accessible from inside the tanks and double bottom, then follow up in dock at Constanța, Varna or Burgas when the ship moves there.
list: The Mangalia shipyard quays and docks — repair and conversion work; early gauging gives a measured steel scope for renewal or repair planning.
Lay-by berths in the commercial harbour — ships waiting for a yard slot or a sale decision; deck, tank and hold measurement alongside.
Heavy-lift and fitting-out quays — offshore support and work vessels under conversion; hull and tank gauging before and after modification.
Anchorage off the port — occasional waiting ships; deck and ballast tank work by launch in settled weather.
Nearby docking alternatives — Constanța to the north and Varna or Burgas to the south take ships that need a dry dock when Mangalia cannot offer one.

context.h: Port state control and the rules around Romanian repair calls
p: Port state control in Romania is carried out by the Romanian Naval Authority, which acts under the Paris MoU and the Black Sea MoU. A ship that arrives for repair after a detention or a serious deficiency will usually need class and the authority satisfied before it sails, and measured thicknesses are often the evidence that settles whether a defective area needs permanent renewal or a temporary repair. Having the figures taken at the start of the stay, not at the end, avoids delays at departure.

For ships heading into or out of Romania, EU rules shape the repair decision as much as the steel does. The Ship Recycling Regulation requires an Inventory of Hazardous Materials on board for ships calling at EU ports, EU emissions trading applies to voyages touching the Union, and FuelEU Maritime now affects how owners weigh the age and efficiency of an older ship. A hull that measures well may justify a docking investment, while one with widespread wastage often leads an owner towards sale or recycling, and a gauging report is the document that supports either path.

jobs.p: The enquiries that suit Mangalia are linked to yard time and to ships whose future is being decided. A repair plan needs measured steel before a quotation can be trusted, and a buyer needs a ship's condition before committing. The work below is typical, and each job is scoped from the survey status, the access the yard permits and the tanks that are empty on the day, then confirmed with the superintendent before the team leaves India.
list: Pre-docking gauging of a bulk carrier or general cargo ship at the yard, so the steel renewal estimate comes from measured figures before the dock is flooded down.
Hull, tank and deck measurement on an offshore support vessel under conversion, recording plate condition before new structure is welded in.
Owner's condition gauging on a ship laid up alongside, to decide between a return to service, a sale and recycling.
Pre-purchase gauging for a buyer inspecting a second-hand coaster or short-sea ship lying at a Mangalia berth.
Repair verification after steel renewal, measuring new and adjacent plate and recording the results for the class surveyor.

logistics: The nearest large airports are Constanța Mihail Kogălniceanu for limited services and Bucharest Henri Coandă, with the rest of the journey by road; Varna Airport across the border is another option for some routings. The yard is a controlled facility, so the ship's agent or the yard's security team issues access for each technician and the gauging equipment from passport details sent in advance. Romania is a Schengen state, so the team travels on Schengen visas; mobilisation from India is timed around the visa decision and the yard slot.

faqs.q: Is there a dry dock at Mangalia for a ship that needs bottom gauging?
faqs.a: The shipyard has historically offered docking and heavy repair, but its operating arrangements have changed, so availability has to be confirmed through the ship's agent for the dates you need. If no dock is free, we gauge what is reachable from inside the tanks and double bottom and then plan the bottom shell for a dock at Constanța, Varna or Burgas.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a ship that is laid up at Mangalia?
faqs.a: Yes. A laid-up ship is easier to measure than a trading one, because tanks are usually empty and nobody is working cargo. The main constraints are enclosed-space entry: tanks need ventilation, gas-free testing and a permit, and if the ship has been idle for a long time that preparation takes longer than the measurement does.

faqs.q: Does the same trip cover Constanța and Varna?
faqs.a: It can. Constanța is the larger port to the north and Varna lies across the Bulgarian border to the south, and both are within Schengen. If your fleet has several ships on this coast, grouping them on one mobilisation from India saves travel and uses each visa better. Send us the list of ships and their expected dates and we will lay out a sequence.

faqs.q: What can be measured on a ship waiting at anchor off Mangalia?
faqs.a: Mostly deck plating, hatch coamings, air pipes, deck piping and any ballast tanks that are empty and safe to enter. Boarding by launch depends on sea state, which in winter can stop work on several days. Hold bottoms and shell below the waterline need the ship alongside or in dock, so those items are usually kept for a berth or a yard stay.

faqs.q: How much notice does a ship repair gauging job at Mangalia need?
faqs.a: Enough for the Schengen visas for the technicians travelling from India, which is the slowest step. As soon as the yard slot or the berth date is firm, send the last thickness measurement report and survey status; we then plan the grid, the staging needed and the gauges before anyone books a flight, and re-plan quickly if the yard dates move.
